end.summary:
• Practised building food chains using arrows.
• Correctly formed chains such as ghaas → tidda → mendhak → saanp.
• Identified that frogs eat insects, and birds may eat seeds and insects.
• Predicted effects of removing snakes, owls, and bees from food chains.
• Plant food-making and the role of plants at the start of every chain were not yet explained independently; teach-back not passed.
end.parentNote: Asha practised food chains with Manav using arrow direction and removal scenarios. They consistently built several chains correctly and explained that fewer snakes can lead to more mice and less grain; an arrow-direction mix-up was corrected during the lesson. At home, ask them to draw one chain and explain what may happen if one plant or animal is removed, including why plants begin the chain.
